text:
Millions of people are living with diabetes(Image: Getty)

A pharmacist is warning people to watch out for a key diabetes symptom which can be easily missed. The early warning sign can often be little thought of with people putting it down to the time of the year.

Diabetes UK figures show there are almost six million people in the UK living with diabetes. This includes more than 4.7million people with a confirmed diagnosis and 1.3million people who are unaware they are living with the life-threatening condition that can cause a range of health issues if not spotted in time.

According to Yorkshire Care Alliance undiagnosed diabetes can lead to a number of major health issues including blindness, heart disease, kidney and nerve damage and amputations.

Being constantly thirsty can be a sign of diabetes(Image: GETTY)

It warned on its website: "Early detection of pre-diabetes is crucial to preventing Type 2 diabetes and its complications. Meanwhile, those unknowingly living with diabetes may not show symptoms for years, but left untreated diabetes can lead to severe health issues affecting the heart, eyes, feet, nerves, and kidneys."

But there is one symptom that appears early which can be easily missed as something else. This can be especially the case in the summer when the weather is warmer prompting people to drink more.

Health experts from Chemist Click say needing to urinate more frequently than usual, particularly when it happens alongside increased thirst or unexplained fatigue could be a key sign that all is not well and needs to be checked out. Abbas Kanani, Superintendent Pharmacist at Chemist Click, says frequent urination is one of the earliest and most commonly reported signs.

Known medically as polyuria, this can occur when high blood sugar levels cause the kidneys to work harder to remove excess glucose from the body, leading to increased fluid loss. He said: "One of the most common early symptoms of diabetes is needing to urinate more often than usual.

"When blood sugar levels are high, the body tries to get rid of excess glucose through the urine, which leads to increased bathroom visits. This can sometimes be most noticeable at night, when people find they are waking up more frequently to use the toilet."

Abbas Kanani, Superintendent Pharmacist at Chemist Click(Image: Chemist Click)

He adds that while this symptom alone does not confirm diabetes, it should not be ignored if it becomes persistent or is accompanied by other changes. He said: "It’s important to look at the whole picture.

"If frequent urination is happening alongside symptoms such as increased thirst, tiredness or unexplained weight changes, it’s worth speaking to a healthcare professional and getting blood sugar levels checked. Early detection can make a significant difference in long-term management."

There are two types of diabetes - type 1 and type 2. While type 2 is the most common around 8% of people with diabetes will have type 1.

Type 1 happens when your body fails to produce enough insulin - a hormone which controls blood glucose (sugar) levels. This needs to be managed by taking insulin daily - usually via injection. It is often diagnosed in childhood but you can get it at any age and it cannot be prevented.

Type 2 diabetes is also caused by a problem with insulin and is often linked to being overweight, inactive or having a family history of the condition. And while serious this too can be managed however this is usually by changes in diet and often medication.

According to the NHS diabetes signs are not always obvious. It says: "Many people have type 2 diabetes without realising. This is because they may not always notice any symptoms."
